newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key points of prosecutors statement on Hamanaka.
newsitem.headline: Key points of prosecutors statement on Hamanaka.

text.p: The following are key points from the opening statement made by the Tokyo Prosecutor"s Office at the first day of the trial of former Sumitomo Corp copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Hamanaka entered guilty pleas on charges of fraud and forgery.
The following is an unofficial translation by Reuters and should not be taken to represent the official wording of the prosecution statement, issued in Japanese:

The defendant began to make unauthorised, off-the-book transactions in 1985, in cooperation with his then-superior, but instead of making profits, ended up deeper in the red by the 1985 fiscal year-end in September.
He continued to hide the losses until they ballooned to some 285 billion yen, or $2.6 billion.
In order to cover those losses, he raised a total of $770 million through fabricated copper warrant deals out of Sumitomo"s Hong Kong subsidiary in October and November 1994.
He also used "commodity financing," loans mortgaged by copper warrants owned by Sumitomo, or borrowed though a system of repurchases by Sumitomo, in futures and options deals.
The defendant raised the money despite the fact that he was not authorised to take out such loans by the internal rules of the company.

He covered up the huge losses from unreported transactions for 10 years by failing to enter any of the information into the in-house computer network. He asked his customers to send confirmation forms directly to him but would then quietly dispose of them.
He was extremely adroit in concealing the enormous debt he held through his copper transactions.

The defendant also submitted false balance sheets to the accounting section of Sumitomo"s copper division by substituting the genuine ones he obtained from customers at his regular monthly book-balancing meetings.

A special audit group for copper and base metals transactions was formed within Sumitomo and operated between November 1991 to December 1992. But as the defendant was appointed the team leader of the group, he was able to keep any incriminating documents from being passed to the group.

The defendant also received 15 million yen ($120,000 at current exchange rates) in cash from the Tokyo representative of British brokerage Winchester Commodities Group, who was a close acquaintance of his.
He used the money to entertain clients and others at night clubs, to buy golf club memberships and to make overseas trips. ---
Because of investigations by British and U.S. regulators, the defendant was removed from his position on May 9 1996.
He finally acknowledged that that he was not able to conceal the evidence of the off-the-books transactions and his enormous debt and admitted everything to his superior on June 5, 1996.
Sumitomo conducted an internal investigation which revealed losses of $2.6 billion.
